terminologyProfile.descriptionRule: Use measurable 3D graphics terms. Avoid vague words unless they are paired with concrete geometry/material/shader parameters.

referenceCamera.note: For likeness work, solve the reference camera (forge/stage1_intake/solve_camera_pose.py) so the review render aligns with the photo and the reference can be projected. Confirm by overlay review.

objectClass.notes: ONE BAY of a modular outdoor roof kit, and the only one of the six whose roof does NOT close: a 4 x 4 m cell on a 4 m grid, four sawn timber corner posts under a perimeter beam and cap rail, and a flat deck of forty-eight spaced bamboo culms that casts a striped shade and lets the sky through. Nothing opens, turns or swings and nothing attaches -- a neighbouring bay is PLACED at 4 m, not socketed -- so one root pivot at base-center and zero sockets. Open on all four sides. The shade frame over a garden table, a guesthouse terrace or a temple forecourt: sawn hardwood posts gone grey-brown with a bamboo deck laid across them, which is the cheapest roof that is not a roof. It shades without enclosing, and it is what a Thai street cafe puts over the pavement when a tarpaulin would look permanent.

reasoning: TWO components and no repetition system: ONE timber merge (four posts, four beams, four cap rails, two purlins, eight post-head cleats) and ONE bamboo merge (forty-eight culms). Two draw calls of four, two unique geometries of six.

The roof is a MERGE and not an InstancedMesh, which is the single most consequential decision on this prop and costs nothing: 1,152 triangles either way. A merge can carry PER-CULM uv offsets, so the node rings fall at a different phase on every culm, and per-culm radius, roll, height and a DIFFERENT tone at each end. An InstancedMesh shares one geometry, so every culm gets the same node stations; thirty-six identical cylinders read as a printed stripe however many tones ride on the instance colour attribute, and that is exactly what the first build shipped.

Two materials of three: weathered timber (three vertex tones -- post, beam, cap rail) and bamboo (seven tones carried at BOTH ends of every culm). Both textureless as declared, each with one 512 px multiply canvas bound after construction.

1,416 of 4,000 triangles. Twelve radial segments on a 70 mm culm is generous and is what the merge buys: nodes are texture, not geometry, because a 6% collar on a 70 mm culm is 2 mm and no ring of triangles resolves it at prop distance.
Action readiness: one root pivot, zero sockets, no declared collider shape, no destruction groups.

specDepthDecision.rationale: The identity is a flat deck of ROUND spaced culms in a dark sawn frame -- the registry notes say so, and say why it cannot be an alpha-cutout deck: seen from underneath at a grazing angle an alpha roof is a row of hard edges, and these culms have depth a player sees from below. Everything else is surface. The node banding, the fibre grain, the sun-faded grey drift, the checking splits in the timber and the rust bleeding from old bolts are all identity in the plate and all of them are two canvases, because none of them changes the silhouette.

detailInventory.note: Enumerate every identity-defining small detail before authoring the spec. Each detail must map to a component.localFeatures entry or material.localOverrides entry, never prose only. Use forge/stage1_intake/build_detail_inventory.py to scan zones.

resolvedUnknowns: Culm DIAMETER is the one measurement taken from reality rather than from the plate. Scaled against its own frame the plate's culms come to about 190 mm at a 4 m bay, which is larger than any bamboo; 70 mm at a 79 mm pitch keeps the plate's measured gap-to-pitch ratio of 0.12 on a culm that exists. Forty-eight of them cross the 3.80 m clear span.

The node rings are TEXTURE, not geometry. A node collar on a 70 mm culm stands about 2 mm proud, which is below what a ring of triangles resolves at prop distance; the tile carries them at 300 mm along a 600 mm culm-uv tile, phased per culm.

Each culm is given a DIFFERENT tone at each end and the vertex colours interpolate between them. A real deck is spliced and one end of a 4 m run gets more sun than the other; the plate's deck varies along each culm as much as across the course.
The post-head cleats sit on the two INNER faces of every post. The plate shows a bracket at the post head on the outside, and nothing on this module may cross the cell edge, so it is carried inboard.
Interior of the timber sections is not modelled and the frame is boxes. A pergola is looked at from outside and from underneath, never from inside a beam.
preSpecAssessment.unknownsResolutionNote: Emptied because every entry has been RESOLVED with a recorded authoring decision, not because the gaps went away. Each is restated in assumptions and in viewEvidence with its confidence and a null path. Nothing was invented to close a gap.

definitionOfDone: Rendered model matches the reference silhouette, the 4.00 x 2.60 x 4.00 m proportions, the visible component hierarchy and the material response for a real-time browser prop.
All four scene-budget ceilings hold: <=4000 triangles, <=4 draw calls, <=3 materials, <=6 unique geometries.
Zero coincident co-facing surface pairs (check-coplanar clean).
Exactly one root pivot plus 0 named mechanism pivot(s); zero sockets; none collider; no destruction groups.
Every material declares textureless with named evidence.

pivotInventory.name: root
pivotInventory.justification: The rigid body of the prop at its declared origin. A named pivot is a promise that a part turns on it, and only real mechanisms get one.

actionReadiness.socketJustification: ZERO sockets, deliberately. Nothing attaches to this prop and nothing is emitted from it. A marker named for a place on the surface is a location, not a mechanism.
actionReadiness.destructionJustification: The asset declares destructionGroups as an empty list -- this prop is NOT breakable. No component carries actionProfile.destruction.fractureGroup. promote-model checks built against declared as an equality in BOTH directions, so an invented group fails the gate just as a missing one would.

coordinateFrame.notes: Origin base-center at ground, +Y up. The culms run along X and the course marches along Z. A neighbouring bay sits at +-4.00 m on X or Z with the same alignment, and the two bays' corner POSTS then pair at the shared edge.

silhouette.description: A 4.00 x 4.00 m bay: four 130 mm sawn timber posts at the corners with their outer faces ON the cell edge, a 195 mm perimeter beam at 2.34 m recessed behind them, a 65 mm cap rail closing the top at 2.60, and a flat deck of forty-eight 70 mm bamboo culms at a 79 mm pitch running along X with a 9 mm gap between them. Two purlins under the deck. Open on all four sides, nothing overhanging.
silhouette.envelopeDerivation: Measured bounds -2.000..2.000 in x and z and 0.000..2.600 in y, i.e. the declared 4.00 x 2.60 x 4.00 exactly. The POST owns the cell edge here, which is the change from the first build: 130 mm posts with their outer faces ON +-2.000, the perimeter beam recessed 10 mm behind them to +-1.990 and the cap rail 5 mm to +-1.995. That is what lets the post head read as a real joint standing proud of the rail it carries while nothing crosses the cell edge, and it is also why check-coplanar is clean at 0.001 m -- three members meeting at a corner with their outer faces on ONE plane is four same-facing coplanar pairs, and stepping them apart costs 10 mm nobody sees. The vertical stack: post 0.000-2.340, beam 2.340-2.535 (195 mm deep, 90 mm thick), cap rail 2.535-2.600 (115 mm thick, so it reaches 65 mm further inboard than the beam), culms centred at 2.5185 with a 35 mm radius so their crowns at 2.5535 are LAPPED 18 mm by the cap rail. The lap is the fix for the defect the first build shipped: with the culm tops flush at the rail line the bay carried an open slot its full width above the outermost culm, which the turntable gate found at azimuth 0 and 180 as a 468 x 2 px see-through sliver. Two purlins run along Z at x = +-0.65 from 2.400 up to the culm undersides, which is what a player standing under the bay actually sees. The PROXY is used for the plan and not for the height: Meshy v7 over the same plate reads square to within 0.04 of its height on all ten bands, and reads 1 : 0.83 : 1.00 against the built 1 : 0.65 : 1.00. The registry notes fix the 4 m cell and the flat 2.60 m roof, so the declared envelope governs, exactly as it does on the other five canopy modules. The one place the PLATE is not followed literally is culm diameter: measured against its own frame the plate's culms scale to about 190 mm at a 4 m bay, which is not a bamboo that exists. 70 mm at a 79 mm pitch is a real culm carrying the plate's own gap-to-pitch ratio of 0.12.
silhouette.meshyCrossCheck: Independent Meshy v7 reconstruction of the same plate (fal, request 01a057e9, ultra_mode, 4,000 target triangles). Band table over ten bands: the proxy reads width 1.177-1.218 and depth 1.173-1.235 of its own height, i.e. w:h:d 1 : 0.83 : 1.00, against the built bay's 1 : 0.65 : 1.00. SQUARE IN PLAN at every band, which is what the proxy is used for and what it settles: width and depth agree to within 0.04 of the height on all ten, so the bay is square and the culms cross a square cell. It is NOT used for the height -- the proxy reconstructs a small slatted TABLE and the registry notes fix a 2.60 m flat roof because a player has to walk under it, so the declared envelope governs and the built bay is proportionally lower than the plate's subject. Mean |delta| is 0.334 of the height in width and 0.342 in depth, which is that decision stated as a number rather than a fidelity failure. The proxy narrows at band 9 (1.195 from 1.217), consistent with the plate's deck sitting inside a perimeter beam rather than overhanging it.

viewEvidence.note: NOT DIRECTLY OBSERVED. Confidence 0.94: the bay is symmetric about both axes and open on all four sides, and the plate shows two full elevations and the whole deck. There is nothing a rear view could carry that the front does not.

componentTree.name: Posts, perimeter beam, cap rail, purlins and cleats
componentTree.topologyRationale: Four posts, four beams, four cap rails, two purlins and eight cleats are one merge and ONE draw call, and the root the deck hangs off. Nothing here moves relative to anything else here.

geometryDescriptor.topologyIntent: Posts 0.130 square, outer faces ON +-2.000, y 0.000-2.340. Perimeter beam 0.090 thick with its outer face at +-1.990, y 2.340-2.535, the +-Z pair running the full width and the +-X pair butting against them. Cap rail 0.115 thick at +-1.995, y 2.535-2.600, reaching 65 mm further inboard than the beam so it laps the culm crowns by 18 mm. Two purlins 0.090 wide along Z at x = +-0.650, y 2.400-2.4835. Eight cleats 0.045 x 0.230 x 0.085 on the two inner faces of every post head.
geometryDescriptor.zFightingNote: NOTHING is flush and co-facing. The three members that meet at the cell edge are stepped 10 mm and 5 mm apart, so the post face at +-2.000, the rail at +-1.995 and the beam at +-1.990 are three planes rather than one; the corner joints are OPPOSED butt faces, which is how solids are meant to meet; the cap rail OVERLAPS the culm crowns rather than meeting them. check-coplanar clean at 0.001 m.
geometryDescriptor.mergeNote: One merged BufferGeometry carrying position, uv and colour. Every member is given its own (u, v) offset in the tile, so two members meeting at a corner never show the same crack and a member longer than the 1.80 m tile does not put its repeat where the eye is already looking.

localFeatures.description: four corner posts owning the cell edge

localFeatures.delivery: eight boxes on two levels, stepped back from the post face
eight boxes on the inner post faces
the timber canvas on world-planar uvs, u along each member

colorMaterialRecipe.recipe: Three weathered timber tones as vertex colours on a WHITE material -- post #5c4b3a, beam #977f66, cap rail #87715c -- with a timber multiply canvas on world-planar uvs whose u follows each member's length.

pivot.name: root
pivot.notes: At the origin the asset declares. A STATIC prop: nothing opens, turns or swings, so one root pivot is the whole mechanism inventory and that is the correct answer, not a gap.

componentTree.name: Forty-eight spaced bamboo culms
componentTree.topologyRationale: Forty-eight culms are one merge and ONE draw call. They are a MERGE rather than an InstancedMesh deliberately and at no triangle cost: only a merge can carry a per-culm uv phase, so the node rings fall at a different station on each culm, and a different tone at each end of each culm.

geometryDescriptor.topologyIntent: Forty-eight open-ended cylinders of radius 0.035 (jittered +-6%) and length 3.800, running along X at y 2.5185 (jittered +-1.5 mm), centres marching along Z at a 0.0792 m pitch from -1.860 to 1.860. Twelve radial segments. Each culm carries its own roll, its own (u, v) phase in the 0.60 m culm tile and a tone at each end.
geometryDescriptor.uvStrategy: culm uvs in metres -- u around the circumference, v along the length, over a 0.60 m tile, with a per-culm (u, v) phase
geometryDescriptor.zFightingNote: The culm crowns are LAPPED 18 mm by the cap rail rather than meeting it, and their ends are buried 100 mm inside the perimeter beam -- which is also why they are open-ended: caps would be 48 x 20 triangles nobody can see. No two culms touch: the 9 mm gap is the whole point of the prop.
geometryDescriptor.mergeNote: One merged BufferGeometry carrying position, uv and colour; the culm uvs are written PER CYLINDER, u around the circumference and v along the length, both in metres.

localFeatures.delivery: the culm canvas at two rings per 0.60 m tile, phased per culm

colorMaterialRecipe.recipe: Seven bamboo tones as vertex colours on a WHITE material, a DIFFERENT one at each end of every culm and interpolated along it, with a culm multiply canvas on per-culm culm uvs.

actionProfile.notes: Rigidly parented to the root. NO pivot and NO socket, deliberately: this part does not move and nothing attaches to it.

roughness.notes: Scalar observed for this surface in the plate. The independently extracted map is kept on disk as evidence and is NOT bound at runtime -- this material is textureless, so the scalar is the runtime value.

albedo.samplingNotes: Measured as the mean of crops/beam.png. extract_pbr_evidence confidence 0.880. The extractor palette is advisory only: these crops are flat material swatches, not isolated objects, so its foreground separation is weak by its own warnings. Albedo is the direct crop measurement.

localOverrides.evidence: crops/post.png and crops/beam.png -- checking splits along the grain and rust bleeding down from old bolts, both visible on every member in the plate; carried as sixteen split strokes and five bolt stains on the 512 px canvas.

evidence: Measured on viewEvidence region-beam (0.88) at #836b56 (luma 110.6, saturation 0.344) on the lit beam, region-beamshade (0.84) at #6f5b4b (94.4, 0.321) on the shaded one, and region-post (0.86) at #3f342a (53.7, 0.331) on the post. The post is 57 levels darker than the lit beam and that VALUE SEPARATION is the finding: this is not one brown, it is a sun-bleached top rail over a rain-streaked beam over a post that has been standing in the dirt.

AUTHORED AS THE INVERSE OF THE HARNESS TRANSFER, probed on this prop rather than assumed: an authored #7d6753 (luma 107) measured back at 83 on the lit beam face and 63 on the shaded one, and an authored #4e4034 (66) measured back at 43 on the post -- a factor of about 0.65 with the shading. Carried at #977f66 beam, #87715c cap rail and #5c4b3a post as vertex colours on a WHITE material, which measure back at 105 / 89 / 51 against the plate's 111 / 94 / 54. The RATIOS are what was matched: deck-to-beam 1.31 against the plate's 1.40 and deck-to-post 2.7 against 2.9.

The first build lifted every timber tone to ONE colour at luma 115 for fear of the turntable's background test, and recorded that as the largest deliberate departure from measurement on the prop. It was not necessary. The test is `distance > 24 from the backdrop OR (saturation > 0.16 and luma < 0.94)`, so it is the CHROMA clause that carries a dark weathered timber: the post ships at a rendered luma of 46-51 with saturation 0.355 and the gate reads it as foreground on both clauses, and passes with no --allow-holes at all.

Textureless as DECLARED: one 512 px timber multiply canvas after construction, on WORLD-PLANAR uvs in metres over a 1.80 m tile with u following each member's own LENGTH axis. That last part is the whole trick -- unwrapped by world axes alone a post takes u = x on one face and u = z on the other, so the grain runs ACROSS a 130 mm face and the post ships ringed like a barrel. The tile was 0.75 m first and put the same bolt stain three times down one post.
textureless.note: Declared textureless so createSculptMaterial skips makeProceduralTextureSet entirely -- FIVE canvases per material written pixel by pixel, at a cost that is the SQUARE of the resolution. It is also a correctness fix: with a texture set the generator forces color to white and roughness to 1 and reads both from the generated maps, discarding this measured albedo.

roughness.notes: Scalar observed for this surface in the plate. The independently extracted map is kept on disk as evidence and is NOT bound at runtime -- this material is textureless, so the scalar is the runtime value.

albedo.samplingNotes: Measured as the mean of crops/culm.png. extract_pbr_evidence confidence 0.900. The extractor palette is advisory only: these crops are flat material swatches, not isolated objects, so its foreground separation is weak by its own warnings. Albedo is the direct crop measurement.

localOverrides.evidence: crops/deck.png -- darker collars crossing every culm at roughly 300 mm with a light sheen above and a fringe of root scars below; carried on the culm canvas at two rings per 0.60 m tile, phased per culm.

evidence: Measured on viewEvidence region-culm (0.90) at #bd9773 (luma 155.1, saturation 0.398) and region-slat (0.88) at #c09773 (157.2, 0.402). The two means agree to two levels and the SPREAD is the finding: p10 88 against p90 195 inside one crop of the deck, which is not shading alone -- the plate's course runs from pale straw through honey to a weathered grey, culm by culm and along each culm.

AUTHORED AS THE INVERSE OF THE HARNESS TRANSFER: an authored mean luma of 164 measured back at 104 on the deck, a factor of 0.634. Carried as SEVEN tones with a mean luma of 192 and a mean saturation of 0.39 -- #e8c286, #ddb67c, #eed4a2, #cfaa78, #e6c288, #d2bd97, #ebcc93, one of them the grey a sun-faded culm has gone. Saturation was the second correction and the one the numbers alone would have missed: at a rendered luma of 130 against the plate's 155 the deck still read PALER than the plate, because its rendered saturation was 0.33 against 0.398. Warming the tones at the same value fixed what raising the value could not -- which measure back at 130-132 against the plate's 155. Each culm takes a different tone at EACH END and the vertex colours interpolate along it.

Textureless as DECLARED: one 512 px culm multiply canvas after construction with CULM UVS -- u around the circumference and v along the length, both in metres over 0.60, written per culm with its OWN (u, v) phase. That is what puts two node rings on every culm at real 300 mm spacing and at a different station on each of the forty-eight; a planar unwrap would ring the whole deck on one line.
textureless.note: Declared textureless so createSculptMaterial skips makeProceduralTextureSet entirely -- FIVE canvases per material written pixel by pixel, at a cost that is the SQUARE of the resolution. It is also a correctness fix: with a texture set the generator forces color to white and roughness to 1 and reads both from the generated maps, discarding this measured albedo.

reviewHistory.summary: Structural pass: posts owning the cell edge at +-2.000, beam recessed 10 mm and cap rail 5 mm behind them, purlins along Z at +-0.65, cleats on the inner post faces.

The roof was 36 InstancedMesh culms at a 103 mm pitch on a 75 mm culm -- a batten roof at three times the plate's spacing, and one shared geometry, so every culm carried the same node stations and the deck read as a printed stripe. Rebuilt as 48 MERGED culms at 79.2 mm with a 9.2 mm gap, the plate's own gap-to-pitch ratio of 0.12, each with its own uv phase, roll, radius, height jitter and a different tone at each end. It costs nothing: 1,152 triangles, one draw call and one unique geometry either way.

The first build left an open slot the full width of the bay above the outermost culm -- the turntable gate found it at azimuth 0 and 180 as a 468 x 2 px see-through sliver -- and had no roof structure at all under the deck. The cap rail now reaches 65 mm further inboard than the beam and LAPS the culm crowns by 18 mm, which closes it; two purlins along Z at x = +-0.65 carry the deck and are what a player standing in the shade sees; eight cleats tie the post heads to the beam.

Three tones restored -- post, cap rail, beam -- measured back at 51 / 89 / 105 against the plate's 54 / 94 / 111, and the gate passes with no --allow-holes at all.

The deck was 12% too dark AND 17% too grey. Value was corrected first by probing the harness transfer on this prop (authored mean luma 164 measured back at 104, a factor of 0.634) and inverting it; the deck still read paler than the plate, because rendered saturation was 0.33 against the plate's 0.398. Warming the seven tones at the same value is what fixed it -- the second correction, and the one the luma numbers alone would have missed.

reviewHistory.summary: Material pass: timber 0.88 and bamboo 0.90, both textureless as declared. Three timber tones and seven bamboo tones, all vertex colours on white materials, all authored as the inverse of a probed harness transfer.

Both materials were bare colour with no surface at all -- no grain, no nodes, no weathering -- against a texture brief that names fibre grain, node banding, uneven grey sun-fade, checking splits and rust bleeding from old bolts. Two 512 px MULTIPLY canvases added after construction, both with a near-white base so the measured albedo stays on the vertex colours.

The timber tile shipped CROSS-GRAIN on the posts and repeated three times down one: unwrapped by world axes alone a post takes u = x on one face and u = z on the other, so the grain ran across a 130 mm face and the post read as a barrel with hoops. u now follows each member's own length axis on every face containing it, the tile is 1.80 m rather than 0.75, and every member carries its own (u, v) phase. Found by zooming the render on a post, not by looking at the tile.

lodPlan.strategy: full component tree and material layers
merge static components and reduce local feature geometry

performanceBudget.optimizationPolicy: Real-time browser FPS prop on low-end integrated GPUs; a level builder places hundreds at once. All four ceilings come from thaikit resolveBudget() for the large class and none was invented. The component split was costed against the DRAW-CALL ceiling in the blockout, before any geometry existed: parts that share a material are merged into one component rather than left to be merged later, because a pivot hung off a part cannot be merged afterwards.

drawCalls.note: Two components and no repetition system: 2 of 4. One timber merge and one bamboo merge.

materials.note: timber and bamboo: 2 of 3. Three timber tones and seven bamboo tones are all vertex colours on white materials.

uniqueGeometries.note: One per component plus one per repetition system. A scaled box is NOT a shared geometry -- the generator bakes real dimensions in via geometry.scale(), so every differently-sized box is genuinely distinct. Each InstancedMesh reuses a single geometry across all its instances, which is the whole point.

triangles.note: 1,416 of 4,000: 1,152 in forty-eight twelve-segment open culms and 264 in the twenty-two boxes of the frame. Twelve segments on a 70 mm culm is generous and is what the merge pays for: the nodes are texture, so no triangles are spent on a 2 mm collar.

lightingFromPhoto.notes: The plate is a flat studio lightbox: surfaces at 90 degrees to each other measure within a few levels, which is only possible under near-shadowless illumination. That is WHY the measured crop means are usable as albedo with little correction.
High fill ratio inferred from the shadow-side wall retaining full value.

The seamless backdrop acts as a large uniform environment. The thaikit harness supplies NO environment map, which is why every metal on this prop carries a metalness well below its physical value -- a metal with nothing to reflect renders black.
NO rim light in the plate. Recorded so a missing rim in the render is not read as a defect.
Exposure 1.0 with ACES filmic tone mapping; no exposure compensation is applied to the measured albedos and none is warranted.

NO contact or ground shadow in the plate -- it is a cut-out against a seamless backdrop. Recorded so the absence is not read as a missing feature. IN USE this is a floor-placed building and the HOST scene owns its contact shadow: castShadow ships enabled on every mesh and the factory defines no ground plane of its own.

proceduralStrategy.strategy: Boxes for every timber member; open-ended cylinders for every culm. No lathes, no sweeps, no extrusions.

NO instancing, deliberately. The forty-eight culms are merged rather than instanced because an InstancedMesh shares one geometry and therefore one set of node stations, and identical cylinders read as a printed stripe. The cost is nil -- 1,152 triangles either way, one draw call either way, one unique geometry either way. In a scene the HOST places whole bays on the 4 m grid.
All procedural variation is assigned by instance INDEX, never from a random source, so the model is byte-identical on every build.

Both materials are declared textureless. Two 512 px multiply canvases after construction, ~2.8 MB of texture VRAM; both are written in MULTIPLIER space with a near-white base, so the measured albedo lives on the vertex colours and the canvas carries nothing but the surface.

risks.description: The proxy reads w:h:d 1 : 0.83 : 1.00 and the built bay is 1 : 0.65 : 1.00 -- a mean divergence of 0.334 of the height in width and 0.342 in depth.
risks.mitigation: The registry notes fix a 4 x 4 m cell on a 4 m grid at a flat 2.60 m, because the grid divides the kit's 8 m ground and road tiles exactly 2 x 2 and because a player has to walk under the roof. The proxy reconstructs a small slatted TABLE, so its height proportion is the plate's subject and not this module's. What the proxy IS used for is the plan -- square on all ten bands, with a band-9 narrowing consistent with a deck sitting inside its beam rather than overhanging it.

risks.description: The plate's culms scale to about 190 mm at a 4 m bay; the build carries 70 mm.
risks.mitigation: No bamboo is 190 mm, so the plate is being read at a scale it was not drawn at. What IS taken from the plate is the gap-to-pitch ratio of 0.12, which is what makes the deck read as nearly-touching slats rather than as battens, and 70 mm at a 79 mm pitch keeps it. Recorded here rather than left as an unexplained difference.

risks.description: Open on all four sides with forty-eight real gaps in the roof, so a lot of what the silhouette encloses is background.
risks.mitigation: It PASSES with no --allow-holes, which the first build could not: enclosed-background fraction 0.000 at azimuth 0 and 180 and 0.008 at 90 and 270 against a 0.010 threshold, largest hole 41 px, silhouette ratios 0.990-0.999. The cap rail's 18 mm lap over the culm crowns is what closed the full-width slot the first build left, and the denser course did the rest.

risks.description: A 1.80 m timber tile repeats 2.2 times along a 4 m beam and 1.3 times down a 2.34 m post.
risks.mitigation: Every member is given its own (u, v) offset in the tile, so no two show the same crack and no repeat lands at a member's midpoint. The first tile was 0.75 m and put the same bolt stain three times down one post, which read as a decal; it was found by zooming the render on a post, not by looking at the tile.
